A folder of suite files is a **directory suite**. To give the whole folder
shared settings — documentation, a suite setup, a teardown — you add an
`__init__.robot` file to it. It holds settings, not test cases.

This chapter's workspace has `checks/` with two sub-suites, `smoke/` and
`catalog/`. Download this lesson's lab, then add an initialization file so the whole
directory shares one suite setup.

## Task 1 — Add a __init__.robot with a suite setup

**Goal:** create `checks/__init__.robot` with documentation and a suite setup
for the whole directory. It has no test cases — it configures the folder.

Here is the same `*** Settings ***` block in a normal suite (with a test so it
runs). Your init file uses the same settings, but drops the test.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Documentation    A folder with a shared setup.
Suite Setup       Log    Preparing the folder

*** Test Cases ***
Placeholder
    Log    ok
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/__init__.robot` exists and defines a Suite Setup.

<!-- hint -->
Create the file at exactly `checks/__init__.robot` — two underscores on each
side of `init`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
In `*** Settings ***`, add `Documentation    Checks directory suite.` and
`Suite Setup    Log    Starting the checks directory`. Add no test cases.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Documentation    Checks directory suite.
Suite Setup       Log    Starting the checks directory
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run the directory suite green

Run the whole directory:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

Robot Framework runs the initialization file's setup once, then the sub-suites.

**Check:** the run finished cleanly (exit code 0).
